statement.p: Use the Divergence Theorem to evaluate the surface integral \iint_{\mathcal{S}} \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{S} .

static.solution: \mathbf{F} = \left\lt x^3,2, z^3 \right>: \text{div} (\mathbf{F})=\frac{\partial }{\partial x}(x^3)+\frac{\partial }{\partial y}(2)+\frac{\partial }{\partial z}(z^3)=3 x^2+3 z^2=3(x^2+ z^2) Using the Divergence Theorem we obtain (\mathcal{W} is the region inside the sphere) \iint_{\mathcal{S}} \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} =\iiint_{\mathcal{W}} \text{div} (\mathbf{F}) \,dV=\iiint_{\mathcal{W}} 3(x^2+ z^2) \,dV We convert the integral to spherical coordinates. We have x^2+ z^2 = \rho^2\cos^2\theta \sin^2\phi +\rho^2 \cos^2\phi =\rho^2 \cos^2\theta \sin^2\phi +\rho^2(1-\sin^2\phi)= -\rho^2 \sin^2\phi (1-\cos^2\theta)+\rho^2 =-\rho^2 \sin^2\phi \sin^2\theta +\rho^2 = \rho^2 (1-\sin^2\phi \sin^2\theta) We obtain the following integral: \iint_{\mathcal{S}} \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} =3\int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{\pi } \int_0^{7} {\rho }^2(1-\sin^2\phi \sin^2\theta )\cdot {\rho }^2 \sin \phi \, d\rho \, d\phi \,d\theta= 3\int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{\pi } \int_0^{7} {\rho }^4 (\sin \phi -\sin^3\phi \sin^2\theta ) d\rho \, d\phi \,d\theta= 3\int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{\pi } \int_0^{7} {\rho }^4 \sin \phi \, d\rho \, d\phi \,d\theta-3\int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^{\pi} \int_0^{7} \rho^4\sin^3\phi \sin^2\theta \,d\rho \, d\phi\,d\theta = 6\pi\left(\int_0^{\pi}\sin\phi\,d\phi\right)\left(\int_0^{7}\rho^4\,d\rho\right)-3\left(\int_0^{2\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\right)\left(\int_0^{\pi}\sin^3\phi\, d\phi \right)\left(\int_0^{7} {\rho }^4 \,d\rho \right)= 6\pi \left(-\cos\phi\bigg|_{\phi=0}^{\pi}\right) \left(\frac{\rho^5}{5}\bigg|_{\rho=0}^{7}\right)-3\left(\frac{\theta}{2}-\frac{\sin 2\theta}{4}\bigg|_{\theta =0}^{2\pi}\right) \cdot \left(-\frac{\sin^2\phi\cos\phi}{3}-\frac23 \cos\phi \bigg|_{\phi=0}^{\pi}\right) \left(\frac{\rho^5}{5}\bigg|_{\rho =0}^{7}\right) = \frac{16807}{5}\left(12\pi -3\pi\cdot\frac43\right)=\frac{134456\pi}{5}
